text:
ria: Quick follow-up from the RFC/rollout — can we do a short postmortem on the telemetry-driven gating that flipped yesterday? The canary failed to detect a tokenization mismatch and we routed traffic to the slowpath. Not a huge outage but woke up customer SREs.

sam: saw it — root cause looked like a mismatch between the runtime tokenizer fingerprint and the ingest descriptor. Perf probes passed but the golden-sample coverage missed the new tokenizer edge-case.

maria: agree. The gating predicate currently is too reliant on macro-level latency/accuracy aggregates. We need a lightweight deterministic compatibility check before running golden evals.

leo: +1. Proposal: add a fast ABI-level check at intake that verifies tokenizer hash, vocab size, and model config fields. If mismatch, block automatic canary and mark for manual review. Very cheap.

ria: sounds reasonable. How would that interact with current probe pipeline? We want to avoid duplicating work and increasing ingest latency.

sam: implementation sketch: run the ABI check in the same intake lambda before any artifact staging. It returns one of: PASS, WARN, FAIL. PASS -> normal flow. WARN -> shadow canary (no auto promote). FAIL -> stop and tag. Sample pseudo-rule:

```
if tokenizer_hash != catalog.hash:
  return FAIL
if abs(vocab_size - catalog.vocab_size) > 16:
  return WARN
return PASS
```

maria: that grammar is good. WARN should also attach a minimal diff artifact (first/last token samples and a small tokenization map) so humans can triage quickly.

leo: we should also log the ABI-check result as structured telemetry so Optimize can surface trending mismatches. Schema: product, model_id, abi_check_result, delta_vocab, probe_id. Minimal fields.

ria: one operational tradeoff: more strict checks reduce bad canaries but increase onboarding friction for experimental forks. Can we gate strictness by team/tier? e.g., allow labs/experimental to bypass WARN->auto-block but still record logs.

sam: yes — add policy bit in intake descriptor: "strict_abi": [true|false|auto]. Default true for hosted/dedicated, false for lab. Auto = use heuristics based on historical golden pass rate.

maria: rollout plan: 1) implement ABI check + telemetry events, 2) run in shadow mode for 48h on a sampled intake (10%), 3) tune warn thresholds, 4) flip to default on. Any objections?

leo: add a quick retro doc before flip that lists metrics we care about: canary failure rate, manual-review volume, onboarding latency p95 delta, and false-positive % on golden evals.

ria: agreed. Also add a small fallback action: if ABI check FAIL but runtime found severe degradation, we should surface a recommended fallback model variant in the intake UI so reviewers can quickly swap.

sam: will prototype the lambda and the telemetry schema today. tagging @onboard-bot to create a retrospective thread and capture the shadow-run metrics.

onboard-bot: Created retrospective ticket: https://redwood.internal/boards/ONBOARD-4829 and scheduled shadow-run window: 4801300000-4801386400.

maria: thanks. I'll prepare the minimal diff artifact extractor and a small triage checklist. Anyone want to pair on the sample selection heuristics?

leo: I can take sample selection (sequence length stratification + rare-token focus).

ria: great — let's sync in 30. Short action list: sam prototype lambda, maria diff extractor, leo sample selector, ria owns retro doc.

sam: ack.
